lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 125, for issues 123 and 124: Select by Pattern remembers your pattern and matches words.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
The dialog now keeps your last pattern and a new Match words checkbox in memory until Thunar quits.
You press Ctrl+S, in any folder of any window.
The box already holds your last pattern, fully highlighted.
Select saves the pattern, but only if it isn't empty. Cancel keeps the old one.
The next dialog, in any window, shows the same pattern until Thunar quits.
A new Match words checkbox is on by default, and is remembered the same way.
With it on, your text is split into words by Search's own code, and an exclamation mark excludes a word.
Each name is tested by Search's match: it must contain every word, in any order.
Then the matching files are selected, the same way as before.
Before, the dialog opened empty and only took wildcards, so a query that works in Search matched nothing.
Both memories live only in the running program. Nothing goes to Thunar's settings, so they're gone when Thunar quits.
The text is highlighted only after the dialog is shown, so GTK doesn't clear the highlight.
It saves what you typed, before a bare word gets wrapped in stars, so reusing it never adds more stars.
The pattern is one shared variable for the whole program, the way Thunar already keeps other app-wide state.
The info icon's tooltip changes to explain whichever mode is ticked.
A box of only spaces selects nothing, and stars and question marks are plain letters in word mode.
Word mode shares the wildcard mode's loop, and Case sensitive and Match diacritics still apply.
With the box unticked, the old wildcard pattern runs exactly as before.
In the test folder, cp 2post and cp !1pre both pick the same three files.
With Case sensitive ticked, capital CP picks only the capitalized file.
With the box off, the old wildcard pattern picks the same three.
But a habitual star dot txt is read as plain text in word mode; untick the box for wildcards.
The PR changes the view and its model, adds two verify scripts, and adds this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
Word mode reuses Search's code, shares the wildcard mode's loop, and keeps memory the way Thunar already does.
In a cloud container, the build passed with only older doc warnings, and the packages installed.
22 of 23 tests passed, the word-mode test among them.
The last-pattern test failed only on a screenshot naming rule; the shot was renamed but not re-run.
CI and the screenshot audit haven't run yet.
The local tests came before the review fixes, so CI's verify run is the one to trust.
A fresh review agent found eight problems: three were fixed and five left as they are.
A translator comment was updated, a new doc comment removed, and two tooltip examples now hold in both modes.
One is for you: word mode on by default reads a habit like star dot txt as plain text, as issue 124 asked.
The rest were accepted: a lost translation, fixed shortcut text, a needed translator note and a little repeated setup.
CI's build, review and screenshots, and a clean run of the last-pattern test, come once the PR is open.
Using it on your own desktop waits for the next build after the merge.
The PR, both issues, and a quick way to try it are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on 123 or 124, so nothing builds on this yet.
A pattern history, or remembering the other two checkboxes, would each need its own issue.
In short: Ctrl+S then Enter repeats your last select, and words work just like Search.
